## [2026-11-15](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-15.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [DiVR: New Evaluation of Learned Block Regeneration for Diffusion Language Models](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17320>)

The new DiVR study evaluates using learned outcome scores to decide when a diffusion language model should regenerate a whole block, keeping the generator unchanged. Its controlled comparisons show how targeted revision can improve average reasoning accuracy with fewer forward passes than the tested search baselines, while documenting limits in calibration and repair reliability.

## [2026-10-13](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-13.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [A Critical Look at Power Sampling when Test Time Sharpening LLMs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13653>)

This study tests whether power-distribution sampling improves reasoning because it faithfully sharpens a model or simply searches for likely responses, and introduces a fine-tuning control that targets that distribution more directly. Its model-dependent results motivate testing inexpensive likelihood-based selection and low-temperature decoding before investing in more elaborate samplers.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:36:31.851Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Test-Time Scaling, Power Sampling, Controlled Evaluation

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/stat.ML/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13653>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery of the October 12 new-submission batch, with inferred availability grounded in the official schedule. Sections 3–5 and Table 1 compare three models on MATH500 and GPQA Diamond; simple selection often matches Power-SMC, while more faithful POWER-RLOO produces both gains and a length-collapse failure.

**Limitations:** Experiments use a 1,564-token generation cap, three models, two tasks and seed 0; results are not a universal rejection of sharpening. Training and inference costs are different. Code is promised upon acceptance; a broad prose claim about beating POWER-RLOO contradicts the Qwen-Instruct GPQA table, so it is not repeated.

## [2026-10-03](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-03.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Decoding Looped Transformers Better for (Almost) Free](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02185>)

LoopCD guides a looped Transformer's next-token prediction by contrasting its final recurrent state with an earlier state from the same forward pass, requiring no additional training or auxiliary model. It improves reasoning and code generation in the tested models, while separate multiple-choice experiments show that this guidance can recover accuracy lost by halving recurrent depth.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-03T10:04:50Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Contrastive Decoding, Looped Transformers, Test-Time Compute

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02185>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Matched checkpoints, prompts, and recurrent depths across four model families support the decoding effect. Reduced-depth multiple-choice experiments report 22.5–48.2% lower analytic forward FLOPs. Submission: 2026-10-01T17:58:38Z; the cs.LG listing confirms the October 2 public batch. Newly discovered in this run's 72-hour lookback, absent from all 64 previously covered works.

**Limitations:** FLOPs describe a 512-token prefill calculation, not measured serving speed. Reduced-depth evidence is limited to multiple-choice tasks; guidance strengths and reference states require screening and depend on architecture. Logit guidance adds a readout pass, while hidden guidance can be sensitive to initialization and excessive strength. No public implementation was verified.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [s1: Simple test-time scaling](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393>)

s1 combines supervised training on a small curated reasoning dataset with budget forcing, which controls when a model stops or continues its thinking at inference time. Its simple open implementation separates training quality from inference-time computation, making it a useful baseline for studying the accuracy and cost tradeoff of longer reasoning.

**Published:** 2025-01-31 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:09:33Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Test-Time Scaling, Reasoning, Budget Control

**Positioning:** established-method

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393>) · [Code](<https://github.com/simplescaling/s1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The March 1 revision includes data-selection ablations, decoding comparisons, and compute-versus-accuracy curves; the authors report AIME 2024 accuracy increasing from 50% to 57% under budget forcing.

**Limitations:** The principal evidence comes from a small set of math and science benchmarks; gains eventually flatten and are bounded by context length, so more thinking is not a guarantee of more reliable answers.
